analysis:
Reviewed the three changed provider-swift engine bridge files, which all concern performance-measurement and deadline-admission logic. They do not touch crypto, attestation, authorization, the prefix cache, or the coordinator WebSocket wire format.

1) EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift (head lines 149-158, 177, 194-203, 241-266): Rate.observe now takes keepsNewest, and the observation time becomes max(at, now) when DeadlineAdmissionFixes.enabled. New helpers coversObservation and observationAge were added. This only changes how the freshness timestamp of self-reported tok/s evidence is computed. One consequence: an out-of-order, older completion no longer rejuvenates or regresses freshness. The data is provider-self-reported and was already untrusted for routing and billing (T-007 class). The change does not widen any trust boundary and does not make unverified rates authoritative. An adversarial provider could already misreport rates, so I identified no new regression.

2) EngineV2Bridge+Accounting.swift (head lines 158-177): updateDecodeTpsEwma now also smooths a decode-shape EWMA (batchRows, tokensPerStep, stepWidth). Invalid shapes are replaced by a default of batchRows 1 via shape.isValid. EWMA arithmetic is on finite values. No injection or overflow surface is visible, but the CBv2DecodeRateShape.isValid definition is outside the supplied evidence.

3) EngineV2Bridge+Admission.swift (head lines 98-106, 123-127): On engines without recovery retirement, the isolated-prefill rate is now resolved through IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve, using a calibrated anchor and an idle-engine check. A decodeRateShape is also passed to the SDK admission policy. This affects availability and deadline-admission accuracy (a DoS/latency concern) rather than confidentiality. The open question is whether the resolve function bounds a fallback or anchor rate so that a stale optimistic rate cannot admit work that will miss deadlines. The implementations of IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate, DeadlineAdmissionFixes and the CBv2 SDK handling of decodeRateShape are not supplied. This does not appear to affect any listed security threat directly, so I flag a limited coverage gap rather than a finding. Also unverified: that the admissionFixes flag is defined and defaults safely.
